method: Current-law overlay pass for South African WO geography, post-2025 Jerez product-law changes, and current IVDP Port category/certification rules. These records supersede older current-law assumptions only where an explicit effective date or current authority source is present.

profiles.name: South African Wine of Origin — February 2026 production-area framework
researchNotes: The February 2026 SAWIS production-area table is the current identity snapshot used by the structured designation registry.
All 152 production-area identities remain reference-only; the WO identity table does not itself establish cultivar, style or product-specific winemaking legality.
Still Bay is represented as a district with Goukou River Valley as a ward in the February 2026 snapshot; obsolete names are not carried forward from older WO booklets unless separately versioned.

profiles.name: Jerez-Xérès-Sherry — current post-2025 Union-amendment framework
profiles.legalClass: DOP — category 1 wine and category 3 liqueur wine
researchNotes: The approved 2025 Union amendment means fortification can no longer be treated as a universal requirement for every current Jerez generoso product.
Fino and related generic product terms therefore require an explicit wine-category/process choice before a simulator can assert fortification.
Manzanilla-Sanlúcar de Barrameda remains a separate DOP and is not folded into Jerez-Xérès-Sherry.

profiles.name: Porto / Port — current category, bottling and certification framework

Vintage.certificationWindow: January through June of the second year after harvest
Vintage.mayEnterMarketFrom: 1 May of the second year after harvest
Vintage.bottlingDeadline: 30 July of the third year after harvest

LBV.bottlingDeadline: 31 December of the sixth year after harvest

researchNotes: This pass strengthens category, bottling and certification facts but intentionally does not promote Port to procedural generation-safe status.
A full procedural Port model still requires complete current grape, benefício, fortification and certification constraints.
